headline: Microsoft Responds to Outcry After Quiet Enterprise Install of Beta 'Photos' App
summary: Microsoft addressed concerns regarding the unannounced installation of a beta 'Photos' app in enterprise environments, sparking user and admin frustration.
details: Microsoft faced an outcry from users and IT administrators after a beta version of its 'Photos' app was quietly installed on enterprise systems without prior announcement or explicit consent. This unexpected deployment caused confusion and raised questions about software management practices within corporate networks.

The unannounced installation bypassed standard IT deployment protocols, leading to concerns about system stability, security, and the ability for administrators to control software environments. Many users reported discovering the beta app unexpectedly, prompting a wave of complaints across forums and social media.

In response to the growing backlash, Microsoft acknowledged the issue and stated it was investigating the matter. The company typically provides clear communication and opt-in processes for beta software, especially within enterprise settings, making this incident unusual.

This event highlights the challenges of managing software updates and beta programs, particularly in large-scale enterprise deployments. IT departments rely on predictable and controlled rollouts to maintain operational integrity and security across their infrastructure.

headline_marked: [[H3-metal brings native MiniMax-H3 inference]] to Apple Silicon, generating video 7x faster
headline: H3-metal brings native MiniMax-H3 inference to Apple Silicon, generating video 7x faster
summary: This new open-source project optimizes MiniMax-H3 inference for Apple's M-series chips, enabling video generation in just 3.5 seconds compared to 26.4 seconds for a reference.
details: H3-metal is a new open-source project providing native MiniMax-H3 inference specifically optimized for Apple Silicon. It significantly accelerates video generation, with a four-pass denoise taking approximately 3.5 seconds on an M5 Max, compared to 26.4 seconds for a 29-pass reference.
The project supports prompt-to-video/audio generation, along with first/last-frame conditioning and ordered Ref2VA image/video/audio references. These features are fully functional end-to-end.

Developers can interact with H3-metal via a command-line interface or an Iris-style interactive session. The session keeps prompt conditioning and video decoder in memory for faster iteration, allowing commands like "!save output.mp4" and "!seed random".

Ongoing work focuses on incremental H3-specific Metal performance and memory optimization for M3 Max and M5 Max chips. The system allows for fine-tuning denoising passes, with 4-7 passes offering a balance between detail, motion, and speed.

Further optimizations include "--use-int8-row-fc2", which reduces complete denoiser forwards by about 2.6% while maintaining visual quality. This option is available in the interactive session via "!int8-row-fc2 on".
